title: Rakhi Sant v. State of U.P. — owner's consent no bar to grant or continuance of supply
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pankaj Naqvi, J.; Naveen Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ allowed; restoration to be considered forthwith in accordance with law.
headnote: Neither the Electricity Act, 2003 nor the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 contains any provision empowering a licensee to refuse to grant, or to discontinue, electricity supply solely because the owner's consent is not forthcoming or a dispute is pending. Supply of electricity is an essential service. Writ allowed; respondents directed to consider forthwith restoration in accordance with law.
facts: The petitioner, residing with her children at Flat No. A-95/E LIG, National Apartment, Shalimar Garden Extension-2, Ghaziabad, sought a mandamus to continue electricity supply after her husband, Madan Pal, with whom she had marital discord, complained to the licensee seeking disconnection. The authorities declined, citing the owner's withheld consent. She undertook to discharge any consumption liability. Counsel for the licensee stated that, if dues were cleared, there was no impediment to restoring supply forthwith.

reusable_constructions.construction: Neither the Electricity Act, 2003 nor the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 contains any provision that permits a licensee to refuse to grant, or to discontinue, electricity supply solely because the owner's consent is not forthcoming or a dispute is pending.
Supply of electricity constitutes an essential service without which the survival of a person would be mere animal existence.

holding_units.topic: owner consent not a bar to grant or continuance of supply
holding_units.holding: A distribution licensee cannot refuse to grant, or discontinue, electricity supply only because the owner's consent is not forthcoming or a dispute is pending: neither the Electricity Act, 2003 nor the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 contains any such bar. The writ was allowed and the respondents were directed to consider the petitioner's request for forthwith restoration of supply in accordance with law.
holding_units.flag: Order cites EA 2003 and the 2005 Code generally; no numbered clause was identified.

principle_tags.application: The husband's withheld consent, and the pending marital dispute, could not justify refusal or discontinuance of supply at the petitioner's flat; the Code and the Act contain no such bar.
Restoration was approached on the footing that electricity is an essential service without which survival would be mere animal existence.

not_decided.point: Existence or quantum of outstanding electricity dues
not_decided.note: The petitioner undertook to clear any consumption liability; the Court did not enquire into arrears and left restoration to consideration in accordance with law.
